extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third-party petitioners, and other stakeholders involved in PTAB post-issuance proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on AIA post-issuance proceedings conducted by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, including inter partes review, post grant review, the transitional covered business method program, and derivation proceedings. Covers filing eligibility and timing, grounds/standards for institution, and statutory timeframes for final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Review (IPR) — scope and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review is a new trial proceeding conducted at the Board to review the patentability of one or more claims in a patent only on a ground that could be raised under §§ 102 or 103, and only on the basis of prior art consisting of patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inter partes review process begins with a third party (a person who is not the owner of the patent) filing a petition after the later of either: (1) 9 months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent; or (2) if a post grant review is instituted, the termination of the post grant review. The patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition. An inter partes review may be instituted upon a showing that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one claim challenged. If the proceeding is instituted and not dismissed, a final determination by the Board will be issued within 1 year (extendable for good cause by 6 months). The procedure will take effect on September 16, 2012, and applies to any patent issued before, on, or after that date. See cited Final Rules and Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 48612; 48756; 48680).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Grant Review (PGR) — scope and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Post grant review is a new trial proceeding conducted at the Board to review the patentability of one or more claims in a patent on any ground that could be raised under § 282(b)(2) or (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post grant review process begins with a third party filing a petition on or prior to the date that is 9 months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent. The patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition. A post grant review may be instituted upon a showing that it is more likely than not that at least one claim challenged is unpatentable. If the proceeding is instituted and not dismissed, a final determination by the Board will be issued within 1 year (extendable for good cause by 6 months). The procedure takes effect on September 16, 2012, and generally applies to patents issuing from applications subject to first-inventor-to-file provisions of the AIA. See General Administrative Trial Final Rules and related Proposed Rules (77 Fed. Reg. entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Program for Covered Business Method Patents (TPCBM) — eligibility and special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The transitional program for covered business method patents (TPCBM) is a new trial proceeding conducted at the Board to review the patentability of one or more claims in a covered business method patent, employing the standards and procedures of a post grant review, with certain exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: for first-to-invent patents only a subset of prior art is available to support the petition. Further, a person may not file a petition for a TPCBM proceeding unless the person or the person's real party in interest or privy has been sued for infringement of the patent or charged with infringement under the patent. The procedure takes effect on September 16, 2012, but only applies to covered business method patents. The program will sunset for new TPCBM petitions on September 16, 2020. See Covered Business Method and Technological Invention Definitions Final Rules and related Proposed Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceeding — purpose, timing, and evidentiary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A derivation proceeding is a new trial proceeding conducted at the Board to determine whether (i) an inventor named in an earlier application derived the claimed invention from an inventor named in the petitioner's application, and (ii) the earlier application claiming such invention was filed without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant subject to the first-inventor-to-file provisions may file a petition to institute a derivation proceeding only within 1 year of the first publication of a claim to an invention that is the same or substantially the same as the earlier application's claim to the invention. The petition must be supported by substantial evidence that the claimed invention was derived from an inventor named in the petitioner's application. The procedure for derivation will take effect on March 16, 2013. See Proposed Rule for Derivation Proceedings (77 Fed. Reg. 7028) and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standards and final determination timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Different proceedings have distinct institution standards and time-to-final decision rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes review may be instituted upon a showing that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one claim challenged. Post grant review may be instituted upon a showing that it is more likely than not that at least one claim challenged is unpatentable. If instituted and not dismissed, both IPR and PGR proceedings result in a final determination by the Board within 1 year (extendable for good cause by 6 months). The TPCBM generally follows PGR procedures (subject to its exceptions). Derivation proceedings require substantial evidence of derivation and are subject to a 1-year filing window measured from first publication of a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner and filing-eligibility rules (who may file and timing windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proceeding has specific eligibility and timing rules for who may file a petition and when it must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR and PGR are initiated by a third party (a person who is not the owner of the patent). IPR petitions may be filed after the later of: (1) 9 months after patent grant/reissue or (2) termination of a post grant review. PGR petitions must be filed on or prior to the date that is 9 months after grant. TPCBM petitions are limited to persons (or their real parties in interest/privies) who have been sued or charged with infringement and the program sunsets for new petitions on Sept 16, 2020. Derivation petitions (for applicants under first-inventor-to-file) must be filed within 1 year of the first publication of a claim the same or substantially the same as the earlier application's claim. Patent owners in IPR and PGR may file preliminary responses to petitions.
